name: SAKE BAR 圓谷 (Sake Bar Marutani)

claims.text: No information about cross-contamination controls is published. Tempura is offered on the à la carte menu, indicating wheat flour is actively used in the kitchen.
Wheat-containing soy sauce appears throughout the menu: in simmered dishes (鶏肉の醤油煮), dressings (醤油麹ドレッシング), grilled items, and course meals. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternatives are mentioned.

The kitchen prepares meat and seafood across all courses. The vegan course is a separate reservation-only offering, but no information about dedicated preparation areas or cross-contact prevention is provided.

Reservations are phone-only; staff can be informed of dietary needs at time of booking. The course menu notes that nut allergies (walnuts) should be disclosed in advance, suggesting some allergy awareness, but no formal allergy protocol is described.
A dedicated vegan course is available on request with 3 days advance notice, indicating the kitchen has the capability to prepare plant-based meals when given adequate preparation time.

name: 郷土素材料理 山人昔楼 (Sanjin Mukashiro)

claims.text: Tempura appears in multiple set courses and à la carte dishes. No information on a dedicated fryer or separation from other fried items.
Aged soy sauce (熟成醤油) is a stated house seasoning used across grilled, simmered, and rice dishes. Miso-based preparations also appear throughout the menu. Both contain wheat.
Charcoal-grilled rice balls with shoyu glaze and soy-glazed bamboo shoots are among listed dishes — standard wheat-containing soy sauce is used.
Fish-based dashi is a foundational ingredient in Japanese kappo cooking and is almost certainly present in soups and simmered dishes even where not explicitly listed.
Multiple sources report that the restaurant accommodates allergy requests when notified in advance. No formal allergy protocol or written allergen menu is documented.

The kitchen uses high-quality ancient salt (古代塩) as a primary seasoning alongside soy sauce, meaning some simply-salted grilled items may be free of soy sauce and wheat — worth asking about specifically.
ランチメニューにフライ定食（揚げ物）が含まれており、同一キッチンで小麦を使用した揚げ物が調理されている。専用フライヤーの有無は不明だが、小麦との接触汚染リスクは高い。
醤油ベースの味付けが標準的な居酒屋・海鮮料理店であり、煮魚・タレ類に小麦を含む通常の醤油が使用されていると考えられる。グルテンフリー醤油（タマリ等）の使用は確認されていない。
全メニューが魚介類・海産物を中心に構成されており、植物性食材のみの調理は現実的に不可能な環境。もずくたこしゃぶの出汁は魚介ベース。
アレルギー対応に関する情報はウェブサイト・口コミ・グルナビのいずれにも掲載なし。食物アレルギーや食事制限がある場合は事前に電話（052-971-3091）で直接確認することを推奨する。
Tempura is a core menu item; no separate fryer is indicated. Shared frying oil is a realistic cross-contamination risk for anyone avoiding gluten.
No wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned on any listing. Standard (wheat-containing) soy sauce is almost certainly used in the tsuyu dipping broth and any seasoned dishes.
Fish-based dashi (bonito) is the expected base for the tsuyu broth at a traditional soba restaurant of this type; no plant-based alternative is indicated.
No allergy-handling policy is described on any source. Japanese-only communication is expected; calling ahead at 052-531-2814 is strongly advised for anyone with dietary restrictions.
Buckwheat (soba) noodles are naturally gluten-free in their pure form; the restaurant's emphasis on quality flour is noted, though the exact buckwheat-to-wheat blend ratio is undisclosed.
Wheat flour batter is used for every dish — there is no separation of gluten-containing and gluten-free cooking at any stage.
Tsuyu-based dipping sauce and seasoning sauces are standard Japanese preparations and almost certainly contain wheat-based soy sauce; no tamari or GF alternative is mentioned anywhere.
All mains contain seafood (shrimp, scallops); dashi is presumed katsuobushi-based with no plant-based alternative mentioned.

name: 四間道レストランMATSUURA (Shikemichi Restaurant MATSUURA)

claims.text: グルテンフリー対応に関する公式記載なし。フレンチのコース形式のため、小麦を含むパン・ソース・デザートとの共用厨房環境が想定される。
フレンチが主体のため通常の醤油使用は低いと考えられるが、野菜テリーヌのポシェに和風だし（鰹ベース）を使用しており、だし系調味料に小麦が含まれる可能性を排除できない。
野菜テリーヌのだし調理に動物性（鰹・魚介）が使用されており、ヴィーガン非対応の可能性が高い。ベジタリアン対応は問い合わせ次第で可能な旨が記載されているが、ヴィーガン対応の明記はない。
アレルギー対応に関する問い合わせ先としてinfo@shikemichi.jpが案内されており、予約時に個別相談を受け付けている模様。ただし公式にアレルギー対応メニューの設定があるという記載はなし。
オーナーシェフが食材の質に強いこだわりを持ち、三重県産有機農園野菜・三河湾の鮮魚・名古屋コーチンなど産地を明示した厳選素材を使用。メニューの透明性が高い。

name: 松月 四間道店 (Shogetsu Shikemichi)

claims.text: Tempura is the sole product of this restaurant; wheat-flour batter is used for all items in shared oil. No gluten-free fryer or batter alternative is documented anywhere.
Tentsuyu dipping sauce is standard at tempura restaurants and typically contains wheat-based soy sauce. No tamari or GF soy sauce option is mentioned.
All items are fried in the same oil as seafood (shrimp, uni, etc.). Vegetable tempura shares the fryer with fish and shellfish.
No allergy handling policy or allergen menu is published. Reservation-first model (phone ahead) means dietary requests can be communicated in advance at 070-8960-4649 or 052-485-4410.
Counter seating directly faces the chef, making real-time communication about ingredients more practical than in a table-service setting.
Dinner courses are prix-fixe and made-to-order at the counter, which in principle allows ingredient substitutions if discussed when booking.

name: 昇龍 by うかい亭 (Shoryu by Ukai-tei)

claims.text: Shared teppan cooking surfaces are used for all courses; no information confirms separation of gluten-containing preparations from other dishes.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (containing wheat) is used in teppanyaki sauces and marinades; no tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned anywhere on official sources.
All courses feature wagyu beef, seafood, and animal-derived stocks; no plant-only cooking surface or preparation area is available.

The restaurant states it collects allergy and dietary restriction information at reservation time: "当店では事前にアレルギーなど召し上がれない食材を伺っております" (We ask in advance about allergies and foods guests cannot eat). Requests made on arrival cannot be guaranteed.
No deep-frying on the teppan, which eliminates fryer cross-contamination as a concern.
